topic.title: Instinct was the buzziest AI agent around — can it survive Muse?
topic.summary: Before there were cute little guys, there was Instinct. In August, the startup got its AI agent to market with an unusual playbook: invite-only, no marketing, and barely so much as a website. And yet, Instinct quickly became the buzziest thing in AI, garnering praise for its straightforward, text message-based interface and its ability to […]
topic.angle: Instinct, an invite-only AI agent that got big on word of mouth with no marketing, now faces Muse, a rival from a bigger name. A startup-vs-giant fight over who wins the AI agent race.

draft.title: Instinct AI agent: $10B startup vs Meta and OpenAI

beats.line: Instinct is worth ten billion dollars with no app. It's an AI agent you text.
It launched in August with no marketing. Then Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots arrived.
You chat over iMessage, WhatsApp, or email. It plugs into your calendar.
Reviewer Allison Johnson had it email her eye doctor and start an Ikea return.

beats.line: It identified a Tjusig from her vague description: vertical, white, with branches.
But it missed a prerequisite class for her son's swim lessons.
